statements.text: Artificial Intelligence continues to upend our economy, our education system, and our world. If responsibly developed, AI has enormous potential to promote the common good and usher in a new era of American technological leadership. At the same time, it presents severe challenges on many fronts, from job loss to wealth concentration to disinformation to energy and water use to national security. Congress must develop a policy framework that promotes and champions America’s AI leadership and encourages responsible AI development to create good-paying jobs, protect the environment, keep kids safe, and ensure that AI promotes prosperity for the working class, not just the wealthy few.
statements.venue: Daniel Biss for Congress campaign website, issues page

statements.text: I'm running to fight for universal healthcare so no arts worker has to choose between their craft and their health, stand firm against the unchecked rise of AI threatening creative livelihoods, and make sure the federal government is a real partner for working people in live entertainment.
statements.venue: Actors' Equity Association endorsement press release

statements.text: Usually, I love it when math is in the news, but what’s happening with AI right now is flat out dangerous. We need Congress to step up now and put guardrails around AI before it’s too late. https://t.co/1sWctVvtNf
We don’t need more data centers, we need Congress to do its job and put guardrails around AI before it causes more damage to our planet, or people and our economy. I oppose this proposal.
statements.venue: Statement to Evanston RoundTable on proposed Evanston data center

statements.text: It's encouraging to see folks like @GregCasar, @BernieSanders and others taking bold steps to be proactive about the threats posed by AI. We're gonna need a lot more of this energy to rein in Big Tech and get us all on a responsible path forward. https://t.co/QS4FUxZ63u

statements.text: I understand that there are going to be continued needs for more data centers over time, perhaps, and that if that can be done in a way with appropriate guard rails, with appropriate safety on the AI side, as well as appropriate environmental and land use and public input guard bills, there may be appropriate ways to do that. In the meantime, we’re seeing something run rampant out of control now, and that’s why I support the moratorium.
statements.venue: League of Women Voters candidate forum, Skokie (reported by Evanston Now)
